title: Rapper Young MC Drops Out of Concert After Learning It Was ‘Trump-Backed’
summary: Have you ever agreed to do something and then found out it wasn’t what you thought? That’s what happened to rapper Young MC, famous for the hit “Bust a Move.” He was asked to perform at a big concert in Washington, D.C., called Freedom 250. He said yes because his good friend Rob Base had just passed away, and he was taking Base’s spot. But soon after the lineup was posted online, fans started leaving angry comments. They said the event was backed by former President Donald Trump, and they called Young MC names for agreeing to play. Young MC was shocked. He says no one told him the concert had anything to do with politics. “I was told one thing and then it was a bait-and-switch,” he explained. A bait-and-switch is when someone tricks you by promising one thing and giving you another. He quickly posted on Facebook that he was dropping out. Other artists, like Morris Day and the Time, also backed out. Young MC says he loves music because it brings people together, not divides them. He doesn’t ask fans who they vote for. He just wants to make people dance. Now he hopes to perform in D.C. someday at a show that’s just about the music.
why_it_matters: This shows how important it is to ask questions before joining an event, because your name might be linked to ideas you don't believe in, just like when you join a club at school.

Donald Trump (who was U.S. president from 2017 to 2021) is a polarizing figure, and many events linked to him become political debates.
Many musicians choose to avoid events linked to political figures because they don't want fans to think they support that politician's views.

WHY: He felt tricked because organizers didn't tell him about the political ties, and he believes music should bring people together, not divide them.
